identity.name: Buenos Aires Times
identity.description: An English-language Argentine news website covering national politics, business and culture for expatriate and international readers.

ownership.ownershipNotes: Launched by Editorial Perfil as an English-language successor to the Buenos Aires Herald. Controlled by the Fontevecchia family, a major Argentine media group.

editorialOrientation.evidence: Commercial Argentine outlet with bylined reporting and oppositional coverage of governments across the political spectrum.
editorialOrientation.source: Ownership and self-description via Official about page; secondary references; feed-level sample

politicalLeaning.evidence: MBFC rates Right-Center and High factual reporting; Grupo Perfil has a market-liberal editorial orientation.

economicPerspective.evidence: Coverage generally favours market reforms, fiscal discipline and investment, reflecting Perfil's editorial line.

internationalAlignment.evidence: Frames Argentine politics through market reform, democratic institutions and Western alignment.
internationalAlignment.source: Ownership, editorial positioning and regional coverage sample

reliability.evidence: MBFC rates factual reporting High and credibility High; established Argentine media group.

externalRatings.notes: MBFC: Right-Center; factual reporting High; credibility High (retrieved 2026-10-25).

intelligence.knownPerspective: English-language Argentine market-liberal voice. Explains national politics through economic reform, investment and democratic institutions, with limited regional breadth.

selectionRationale: The only existing English-language Argentine source and a key Latin America gap-filler, though it cannot represent the region alone.

research.researchNotes: Existing production mapping retained. Wikipedia's Buenos Aires Times lookup resolves to Perfil, so ownership was verified via Media Ownership Monitor and the launch essay. Research is feed-level only; full article sampling and peer review remain outstanding.
